questions.stem: A multi-task job got slower last week. The engineer wants task durations and the compute each task ran on, across all runs, in SQL. Which source fits best?

options.A: The driver log of the last run
options.B: system.access.audit
options.C: system.billing.list_prices
options.D: system.lakeflow.job_task_run_timeline

questions.explanation: job_task_run_timeline tracks task-level timing and compute for every run, so you can trend durations and correlate them with compute. Driver logs cover a single run.
questions.evidence: job_task_run_timeline tracks task timing and compute.

questions.stem: Users report intermittent slowness across several serverless SQL warehouses. To find the slowest statements, who ran them and on which warehouse over the past day, what should the engineer query first?

options.A: system.access.audit
options.B: system.query.history
options.C: system.compute.warehouse_events
options.D: system.billing.usage

questions.explanation: query.history records every statement on SQL warehouses and serverless compute, with duration, user and warehouse. warehouse_events covers scaling and start/stop events, not individual queries.
questions.evidence: Captures records for all queries run on SQL warehouses and serverless compute.

questions.stem: A job has tasks T1 → T2 → T3, plus T4, which depends only on T1. In the last run T1 and T4 succeeded, T2 failed, and T3 was skipped. What does Repair run execute?

options.A: All four tasks
options.B: T1, T2 and T3
options.C: T2 and T3 only
options.D: T2 only

questions.explanation: Repair re-runs only the unsuccessful tasks and their dependents. Successful tasks (T1, T4) aren't re-run.
questions.evidence: successful tasks and any tasks that depend on them are not re-run.

questions.stem: A failed task had already appended half its rows to a Delta table before crashing. After Repair run, the table contains duplicates. Why?

options.A: Repair re-runs each unsuccessful task from the beginning
options.B: Repair replays the failed task's writes from its checkpoint
options.C: Repair also re-runs successful upstream tasks
options.D: Delta disables transaction isolation during repairs

questions.explanation: A repaired task starts over, so design tasks to be idempotent (MERGE, overwrite by partition or replaceWhere, txnVersion) so repairs and retries are safe.
questions.evidence: A repair re-runs each unsuccessful task from the beginning.

questions.stem: A task failed because the job parameter run_date was set to a bad value. How can the engineer fix the run without re-running the successful tasks?

options.A: Edit the job's default run_date, then Run now
options.B: Run now with a run_date parameter override
options.C: Repair run, after editing the job's default run_date
options.D: Repair run with run_date overridden in the dialog

questions.explanation: Repair run re-runs only failed tasks and their dependents, and its dialog overrides parameters for that repair. Run now starts over from scratch, and editing the job's defaults changes every future run.
questions.evidence: Parameters you enter in the Repair job run dialog override existing values.

questions.stem: A pipeline table uses expect_or_drop. The team wants the number of rows dropped per update for trending. Where is this metric?

options.A: In system.billing.usage for the pipeline's updates
options.B: In the event log's flow_progress data_quality details
options.C: Only in DESCRIBE HISTORY operationMetrics per table
options.D: In the Spark UI SQL tab of the pipeline cluster

questions.explanation: The event log stores the dropped-record count in the flow_progress.data_quality object, separate from per-expectation pass and fail counts. Query it via event_log() or the published table.
questions.evidence: The metric for the number of dropped records is stored in the details:flow_progress.data_quality object.

questions.stem: A developer runs `databricks bundle deploy -t dev`. The job appears as '[dev jane] nightly_etl', but its daily schedule never fires. Why?

options.A: Development mode pauses all schedules and triggers on deployed resources
options.B: Dev targets can't create jobs with schedules
options.C: The schedule requires a service principal run_as
options.D: The bundle needs `databricks bundle run` before schedules activate

questions.explanation: mode: development prefixes names with [dev user] and pauses schedules and triggers, so dev deployments don't run on their own. Unpause a specific job with pause_status if needed.
questions.evidence: Pauses all schedules and triggers on deployed resources such as jobs or quality monitors.

questions.stem: A CI job deploys `-t prod` (mode: production, git branch: main) from a feature branch, and the deploy fails validation. What is the cause, and what is the recommended setup?

options.A: Production mode requires the target's Git branch; deploy from main
options.B: Production targets can only be deployed through the workspace UI
options.C: The prod target is missing its workspace host setting
options.D: Production mode requires every pipeline to be development: true

questions.explanation: Production mode checks the Git branch (override with --force), requires pipelines to be development: false, and Databricks recommends a service principal as run_as.
questions.evidence: Validates that the current Git branch is equal to the Git branch that is specified in the target.

questions.stem: A bundle target uses mode: development, sets a preset to keep schedules unpaused, and one job sets pause_status: PAUSED. What is the final state of that job's schedule?

options.A: Unpaused; presets take precedence over everything
options.B: Unpaused; the target's mode setting always wins
options.C: Deployment fails because the settings conflict
options.D: Paused; resource settings override presets and mode

questions.explanation: Precedence: the mode's defaults, then presets, then individual resource settings.
questions.evidence: presets override the default mode behavior, and settings of individual resources override the presets.

questions.stem: A team deploys notebooks to production by having engineers click Pull in a shared Git folder. What do the Databricks docs recommend for the production Git folder pattern?

options.A: Let each engineer keep a personal production folder
options.B: Grant everyone CAN MANAGE on the production folder
options.C: An admin-owned production Git folder, updated only by automation
options.D: Export notebooks as DBC files on every release

questions.explanation: Production Git folders sit outside user folders, are admin-owned, and are updated by automation on merge. Most users get run-only access.
questions.evidence: should be updated only by automation when PRs are merged into deployment branches

questions.stem: A team must deploy notebooks, a Python package, two jobs and a pipeline consistently across dev, staging and prod. Today they sync code with a production Git folder only. What do the docs recommend?

options.A: Git folders plus a jobs JSON export per workspace
options.B: Declarative Automation Bundles with per-target settings
options.C: Terraform for jobs, with code synced through Git folders
options.D: Databricks CLI workspace import per environment

questions.explanation: Bundles are the recommended way to deploy code and resources together per target. Terraform plus Git folders can work, but it splits code and resource deployment, which bundles were designed to unify.
questions.evidence: Databricks recommends Declarative Automation Bundles to package and deploy CI/CD workflows.

questions.stem: Automation that updates the production Git folder after each merge should run as which identity?

options.A: A workspace admin user with a personal access token
options.B: A shared account owned by the release team
options.C: The PR author's identity via user-to-machine OAuth
options.D: A service principal with a Git credential for the repo

questions.explanation: Use a service principal configured with a Git credential, so deployments don't depend on a person's account or credentials.
questions.evidence: Create or use a service principal and configure a Git credential so it can access that repository.

questions.stem: The analysts group must read every current and future table and view in schema sales.gold, and nothing else. Which grants follow least privilege?

options.A: SELECT on schema sales.gold only
options.B: USE CATALOG, and SELECT on each existing table
options.C: USE CATALOG, plus USE SCHEMA and SELECT on the schema
options.D: USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and SELECT on the catalog

questions.explanation: Schema-level SELECT covers the schema's current and future objects. The usage privileges are still needed to reach them. A lacks the usage grants, B misses future tables, and D grants the whole catalog.
questions.evidence: automatically grant SELECT on all current and future tables and views in the schema

questions.stem: A service principal has USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and MODIFY on table ops.events, yet its MERGE INTO ops.events fails with a permission error. What is missing?

options.A: SELECT on ops.events
options.B: MANAGE on ops.events
options.C: Ownership of the ops schema
options.D: EXECUTE on the MERGE command

questions.explanation: MODIFY allows insert, update and delete, but also requires SELECT on the table, and MERGE reads the target too.
questions.evidence: Insert, update, and delete data in a table

questions.stem: A data steward must grant and revoke access on catalog finance without becoming its owner. An admin grants them ALL PRIVILEGES, but they still can't manage grants. Why?

options.A: Grants can only be managed by metastore admins
options.B: ALL PRIVILEGES applies only to existing objects
options.C: The steward also needs BROWSE
options.D: ALL PRIVILEGES excludes MANAGE

questions.explanation: MANAGE lets a principal manage privileges (and more) on an object without owning it. ALL PRIVILEGES doesn't include MANAGE (or EXTERNAL USE and READ METADATA).
questions.evidence: does not include the EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA, EXTERNAL USE LOCATION, MANAGE, or READ METADATA privileges

questions.stem: An ABAC column-mask policy targeting the governed tag pii=email is attached to catalog crm. Next week a new table with an email column tagged pii=email is created in crm.marketing. What happens?

options.A: The new column is unmasked until someone runs ALTER COLUMN SET MASK
options.B: The policy applies automatically
options.C: The policy only applies to tables that existed when it was created
options.D: The table creation fails until it is added to the policy's table list

questions.explanation: ABAC policies are evaluated against governed tags, so any securable under the policy's scope that has the tag is covered automatically, including new objects. That's why ABAC scales better than per-table masks.
questions.evidence: that policy takes effect automatically

questions.stem: Why should ABAC masking be driven by governed tags rather than free-form table tags?

options.A: Free-form tags can't be applied to individual columns
options.B: Governed tags are evaluated faster at query time
options.C: Their allowed values and assigners are centrally controlled
options.D: Free-form tags expire automatically after 30 days

questions.explanation: ABAC attributes are governed tags. Controlled values and assignment permissions make the tag itself a trustworthy security control.
questions.evidence: Must use values defined in the associated tag policy.

questions.stem: Analysts must join customer data across tables on email, but must not see the real addresses. The privacy group must see cleartext. Which implementation satisfies both?

options.A: A column mask returning sha2(email, 256) for non-privacy users
options.B: Drop the email column and give analysts a lookup table
options.C: A column mask returning NULL for every user, privacy included
options.D: A row filter keeping only rows where email IS NOT NULL

questions.explanation: A deterministic hash pseudonymizes the value: it stays joinable but isn't readable. The mask is conditional on group membership. Suppression (NULL) breaks the joins, and a row filter doesn't mask columns.
questions.evidence: Table-level column masks are bound to a column using ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET MASK

questions.stem: After adding a table-level column mask to patients.ssn, a data scientist's query `SELECT * FROM patients VERSION AS OF 120` starts failing. Why?

options.A: The mask function lacks EXECUTE for the scientist
options.B: Version 120 was vacuumed when the mask was added
options.C: Masks apply only to current data, so old versions must be unmasked first
options.D: Time travel isn't supported on tables with table-level row filters or column masks

questions.explanation: Time travel and clones are unsupported on tables with table-level filters or masks. Plan reproducibility (for example, snapshots into governed tables) accordingly.
questions.evidence: Time travel isn't supported with table-level row filters or column masks.

questions.stem: A company has 900 tables across catalogs and doesn't know which columns hold PII. They want the PII found automatically and then masked consistently in batch and streaming tables. What should they use?

options.A: A nightly regex job over column names that writes a CSV
options.B: Data classification tags, plus ABAC mask policies on them
options.C: Dynamic views with masking logic over every table
options.D: Manual tagging by each table owner, reviewed quarterly

questions.explanation: Data classification detects PII and applies classification tags, recording results in a system table. ABAC policies keyed on those tags then mask the columns everywhere, including tables that streaming pipelines write to.
questions.evidence: Data classification creates a system table named system.data_classification.results

questions.stem: An engineer wants to enable data classification on catalog hr. What is required?

options.A: A classic all-purpose cluster running continuously
options.B: Workspace admin rights and an external location
options.C: Serverless compute, plus ownership of or MANAGE on the catalog
options.D: Predictive optimization disabled on the catalog

questions.explanation: Data classification runs on serverless compute and is enabled per catalog by its owner or a principal with MANAGE.
questions.evidence: Your workspace must have serverless compute available

questions.stem: A GDPR erasure request is handled with DELETE FROM users WHERE user_id = 42 on a table with deletion vectors enabled, followed by VACUUM. An audit shows the row is still in a data file. What step was missed?

options.A: REORG TABLE users APPLY (PURGE) before VACUUM
options.B: OPTIMIZE users ZORDER BY user_id before VACUUM
options.C: Disabling change data feed on users before VACUUM
options.D: VACUUM users RETAIN 0 HOURS instead of the default

questions.explanation: With deletion vectors, DELETE only marks rows. REORG ... APPLY (PURGE) rewrites the affected files, and VACUUM (after the retention period) removes the old ones.
questions.evidence: REORG TABLE ... APPLY (PURGE) to permanently delete underlying records

questions.stem: After GDPR deletes on silver.users, a downstream Structured Streaming job reading silver.users as a stream fails. What is the recommended fix?

options.A: Recreate the stream with a fresh checkpoint after every delete
options.B: Convert the downstream job to a nightly batch overwrite
options.C: skipChangeCommits on the stream; propagate deletes separately
options.D: Disable deletion vectors on silver.users before deleting

questions.explanation: Delta streaming sources fail on non-append changes. skipChangeCommits skips updates and deletes, so the deletion must be applied downstream by its own process (or use CDF-aware logic).
questions.evidence: skip anything other than inserts, such as updates or deletes.

questions.stem: A retention policy requires that erased customer data be physically unrecoverable within 14 days of a request. A daily job runs DELETE and then VACUUM with default settings (no deletion vectors). Does this comply?

options.A: No; VACUUM never removes files holding deleted rows
options.B: Yes, once the default 7-day VACUUM retention has passed
options.C: Only if time travel retention is extended to 30 days
options.D: No; GDPR deletes must be performed with OPTIMIZE

questions.explanation: DELETE unreferences the rows. VACUUM removes the unreferenced files older than the retention (7 days by default), after which time travel can't reach them. So the data is gone within about 8 days.
questions.evidence: By default, this reduces the time travel capabilities to 7 days.

questions.stem: The governance team needs every table tagged data_owner with values only from an approved list of team names, and only stewards may assign the tag. Which feature fits?

options.A: A free-form tag with a documented list of values
options.B: A column comment holding the owner's team name
options.C: A system tag applied by data classification
options.D: A governed tag with a tag policy for values and assigners

questions.explanation: Governed tags are account-level, enforce allowed values, and limit who can assign them. Free-form tags and properties enforce nothing.
questions.evidence: Must use values defined in the associated tag policy.

questions.stem: An engineer needs a SQL query that lists every column tagged pii across a catalog to feed a governance report. Where should they query?

options.A: <catalog>.information_schema.column_tags
options.B: <catalog>.information_schema.columns
options.C: system.data_classification.results
options.D: <catalog>.information_schema.table_tags

questions.explanation: Column-level tags are in information_schema.column_tags. table_tags covers table tags only. data_classification.results lists what classification detected, not every manually applied pii tag.
questions.evidence: Query the following to retrieve tag information:

questions.stem: Business users must be able to find tables and read their descriptions in Catalog Explorer, and request access, without being able to query any data. Which privilege fits?

options.A: USE CATALOG on the catalog
options.B: BROWSE on the catalog
options.C: USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA
options.D: SELECT on the information_schema

questions.explanation: BROWSE allows discovering objects and metadata and requesting access, with no data access and without USE CATALOG or USE SCHEMA.
questions.evidence: Discover objects, view their metadata, and request access to them without needing USE CATALOG or USE SCHEMA

questions.stem: An analyst was granted SELECT on schema retail.gold but gets a permission error querying retail.gold.sales. No other grants exist. What is missing?

options.A: SELECT granted directly on retail.gold.sales
options.B: USE SCHEMA on retail.gold
options.C: USE CATALOG on retail and USE SCHEMA on retail.gold
options.D: BROWSE on the retail catalog

questions.explanation: Schema-level SELECT does inherit to its tables, but both USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA are needed to traverse to them. B alone still fails at the catalog level.
questions.evidence: does not grant access to the catalog itself or to any specific objects within it

questions.stem: A new 800 TB clickstream table will be filtered mostly by event_date and tenant_id. The team debates PARTITIONED BY (event_date, tenant_id). What does Databricks recommend?

options.A: CLUSTER BY (event_date, tenant_id)
options.B: PARTITIONED BY (event_date) CLUSTER BY (tenant_id)
options.C: PARTITIONED BY (event_date), ZORDER BY tenant_id
options.D: PARTITIONED BY (event_date) with CLUSTER BY AUTO

questions.explanation: Liquid clustering is recommended for all new tables and can't be combined with partitioning (B and D are invalid). Partitioning plus ZORDER is the legacy pattern it replaces.
questions.evidence: Databricks recommends liquid clustering for all new tables, including streaming tables and materialized views.

questions.stem: A liquid-clustered table is fed by a streaming job that commits small micro-batches. Query skipping degrades over the day. Why, and what keeps file sizes balanced?

options.A: Streaming writes disable liquid clustering; switch to partitioning
options.B: Deletion vectors fragment the files; disable them
options.C: The table also needs ZORDER alongside clustering
options.D: Small commits skip clustering on write; OPTIMIZE clusters them

questions.explanation: Small writes don't meet the clustering-on-write threshold. Incremental OPTIMIZE, ideally run automatically by predictive optimization on UC managed tables, compacts and clusters the new data.
questions.evidence: Clustering on write only triggers when data in the transaction meets a size threshold.

questions.stem: Analysts keep creating new views to slice 'net revenue' by different dimensions, and the numbers disagree. What makes a Unity Catalog metric view better here than a standard view?

options.A: A metric view caches every possible GROUP BY result
options.B: Its measures are defined once, separately from dimensions
options.C: It allows writes back to source tables
options.D: It is the only view type that supports row filters

questions.explanation: A standard view fixes its aggregation and grouping when it's created. A metric view defines measures independently of dimensions, so one governed definition works at any grain.
questions.evidence: users can group by any available field

questions.stem: Dashboards built on a metric view are slow on a large star schema. The team wants faster queries without changing the dashboards' SQL. What should they do?

options.A: Replace the metric view with a materialized view
options.B: Add a standard view that pre-joins the star schema
options.C: Enable materialization on the metric view
options.D: Enable query result caching on the warehouse

questions.explanation: Metric view materialization pre-computes aggregates, and queries are rewritten to use them automatically, so the dashboards don't change. Replacing the metric view would lose the governed definitions and require SQL changes.
questions.evidence: automatically rewrites queries to use materialized views when appropriate.

questions.stem: In a star schema, a gold aggregate of sales by store and week feeds many dashboards and is refreshed daily. It must stay correct when late facts or dimension corrections arrive, while recomputing as little as possible. Which object fits?

options.A: A materialized view with a scheduled refresh
options.B: A streaming table with an append-only aggregation
options.C: A metric view queried directly by the dashboards
options.D: A Delta table rebuilt nightly with CREATE OR REPLACE

questions.explanation: An MV stores results and refreshes incrementally where possible, staying correct when inputs change. A nightly rebuild is correct but recomputes everything. A metric view without materialization computes at query time, and a streaming table won't revisit changed history.
questions.evidence: Databricks processes only the data needed to keep the view current; updates are often incremental.
